system.summary: Simple substitution of German in numbers 2-96, one number per letter (90 and 96 both s; 26 = u/v; 15 = i/j), numbers separated by colons and words by a cross; a nomenclator of capital, Greek and doubled letters (Λ Eure Excellenz, Φ Königliche Majestät, Σ Kaiserliche Majestät, XX alliance, ZZ defensiv, YY offensiv, X Auersperg, W Bremen, m Pommern ...), sometimes with figures as suffix. The same key enciphers French in the Prague letter of October 1657.
system.notes: 90 occurs only once in the original letters; 96 is the usual s. Letters are often written twice (original and copy) in the volume. Distinct symbols counted in the originals: 30 numbers and 75 nomenclator symbol forms as transcribed (some forms are variants of one symbol).

prior_solution.where: In the volume: decipherments of the time (img 112-113 for img 110/109; img 157 right-158 left for L18; img 169 right for L25), interlinear decipherments over img 132, 136, 138, 140 and 171, and 19th-century notes in Danish (img 124-125, 137, 138, probably by E. Gigas). In print: summaries in Danish only, E. Gigas, Grev Bernardino de Rebolledo (1883), pp. 282-297, and J. A. Fridericia, Adelsvældens sidste Dage (1894), pp. 238-245 and n. 62, who thanks Gigas for a private decipherment of Sehested's letters, never printed; one German phrase is quoted ("die Gemüther alhie nicht wenig ermunteret"). DECODE, Tomokiyo, Lasry: no entry (11 Nov 2026). The German text of the cipher passages is not in print as far as we found.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target and set the rules (protocol and held-out lines hashed before the measurement; one measurement). Claude Opus 5.5 agents recorded the key on the interlinear decipherment of img 132, checked it on the clear of img 112, transcribed the 27 letters in seven batches, decoded, read and wrote up. No human checked the transcription or the reading.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout (key relevé, measurement, transcription, reading, write-up)

solution.what: Letter values recorded word by word on the interlinear decipherment of the time over img 132; checked on img 110 against the clear of the time img 112 (30 words, word for word).
One pre-registered measurement on held-out lines (img 145 left, 318 numbers): letter score -2.023 vs best of 900 controls -3.693; word-list share 0.569 vs 0.078; 1 number outside the key.
27 letters (and 5 cipher copies) transcribed number by number by seven agents, about 43,000 numbers.
Decoded mechanically and read by sense: 6013 cipher words, 5903 certain, 90 probable, 19 restored, 1 unresolved; copies agree with originals at 76-98% of words.

Project verification and integration of PR #412. Hashes of the five frozen files match; the held-out lines (318 numbers, 51 words, 1 outside the key) decode to the same string with an independent decoder; all 27 letters and 5 copies re-decoded (1,707 of 1,793 lines identical, the rest differ only in printing); about 300 numbers on img 116 and 145 compared with the images: 0 number disagreements, one symbol corrected (img 145 line 3, Φ not Ψ). The contributor's C1/C2 figures could not be re-run (model pickle and corpus not sent); own controls with the repository's de-modern model: -2.615 vs -6.861 (500 permuted keys). Strict recount from reading.md with symbols counted: 6,267 of 6,573 tokens = 95.3%, 12 letters under 95%: class set to read in part, key partial. Three probable words of L01 seen on img 110 as transcribed. The 'Sehested keys 1650-70' (Daisy heid 1449582) recorded as untested.

Claims review by a second reader, settled on the images. The sign X had been given as Kurz from a reading 'H: von Kurtz' of the clear copy img 157 right. Images 157 (id 48703448), 112-113 (48703403-4), 132 (48703423), 158 and 169 were fetched and read: img 157 right line 2 has 'hatt mihr der F: von Auersp: eine weitlaufftige deduction'; img 112 line 5 and img 113 lines 4 and 9-10 have 'Fürst von Aursberg' at the three places where L01 has X; the gloss over X on img 132 right line 1 is a ducal title ('Hertzog von S...', last word not read with certainty). No 'Kurtz' was found on img 112-113, 157-158 or 169. X = Auersperg in key.tsv, reading.md, the summaries and the profile. Recount: [gg]:96 of L13 is an attested symbol (was uncounted), X of L08 (feminine) is diversion by the sense, X of L21 (masculine, marked diversion) is Auersperg: 6,268 of 6,574 tokens = 95.3% (was 6,267 of 6,573); L08 92.7% (was 93.3%), L21 98.3% (was 96.6%).

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The 25 letter values come from the interlinear decipherment of the time on img 132 (19 of the first 23 were already in the project's sweep note of 11 Nov 2026; the contributor added 8 k, 16 p, 36 x, 90 s from the same gloss, then 20 q and 24 y) and were confirmed on the clear of the time img 112. Nomenclator values: 13 from glosses and clears of the time, about 25 by the sense or one attestation, about 26 symbol forms open. L01, L18 and L25 have clears of the time and L27 a full letter-by-letter gloss: for these four the text is in effect read from an existing decipherment, checked against the decode. Stated plainly: the key was extended here, not recovered. No value was obtained by analysis of the ciphertext; the alphabet was copied from the gloss and six letters and the sign values were added to what the sweep note had. The category is the one the README gives for a key taken from plaintext lying beside the cipher. The sign X is Auersperg: the clear copies of the time write "Fürst von Aursberg" three times where L01 has X (img 112-113) and "der F: von Auersp:" where L18 has it (img 157 right), seen on the images on 12 Nov 2026; the contributor had read the place as "H: von Kurtz".
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading.md, strict count of 12 Nov 2026 (strict_count.py): tokens = cipher words + nomenclator symbols of the 27 original letters = 6574; read = 5,903 certain words + 365 symbols whose value a gloss or clear of the time gives = 6268 (95.3%). Holes: 90 probable words, 19 restored, 1 unresolved, 152 symbol values given by the sense, 44 open symbols. The contributor's own figure, 99.7%, counts cipher words only (certain + probable of 6,013) and leaves the symbols out. Recount of 12 Nov 2026 after the claims review: [gg]:96 of L13 counted as an attested symbol (it was in neither class), the X of L08 moved to diversion (by the sense) and the X of L21 to Auersperg (attested); before that the figures were 6,267 of 6,573.

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (protocol SHA-256 525288c0...; held-out transcription SHA-256 e2b4b59e...): pass by its own criteria. Reservations: the agent knew the key while transcribing the held-out lines; the order of events is by the contributor's record (one commit, no outside timestamp); the letter-model pickle and the Merian corpus were not sent, so the C1 and C2 figures (-2.023 vs -3.693; 0.569 vs 0.078) could not be re-run. The project's verification of 12 Nov 2026 re-decoded the held-out lines (identical string) and scored them with the repository's de-modern model: -2.615 vs -6.861 (best of 500 permuted keys) and -6.588 (best of 300 shuffles). The key comes from a contemporary gloss, so the test confirms it rather than establishes it.

credits.note: transcription of 27 letters, key extended (8 k, 16 p, 36 x, 90 s, 20 q, 24 y; about 25 nomenclator values by the sense), held-out measurement, reading and per-letter summaries: Brice Dudout with AI agents (his NOTES name them)

gaps.item: 152 nomenclator tokens whose value is given by the sense or by one attestation (about 25 symbols: Ψ, Ω, ii, a, L, Y, xx, A, B, Z, hh, mm ...) and 44 tokens of open symbols (b, H, bb, cc, Γ, EE, O, R, M, N, Q, F, J, ∂, ww, yy ...)

gaps.item: 90 probable words (one figure off, e.g. grssem for grossem), 19 restored words and 1 unresolved word (copeilig, L14)
gaps.detail: Blots, binding and figures that give a non-word. Three of the probable words of L01 were looked at on img 110 at integration (beidis, miiner, auftrkgen): the figures stand on the page as transcribed, so they are the encipherer's slips, emended by the sense. The rest were not rechecked on the images.

The date on the page reads 28/7; Gigas gives 17 Feb. Not settled from the film. (The other half of this item, Kurz or Auersperg for the talk of 17 March, was settled on the images on 12 Nov 2026: the clear copies write Auersperg, as Fridericia has it.)

texts.label: L01, to the chancellor, Vienna 17/27 Jan. 1657 (with P.S.)
texts.summary: Sehested refers to his letter to the king; Auersperg, at first surprised that no one came with full powers, took the matter up seriously on 14/24 Jan after conferring with La Fuente and gave the enclosed answer; Sehested asks the chancellor for the promised papers. P.S.: a breach between the Emperor and France is expected; forced levies; the French army put at 50,000; Rákóczi already in Poland, for himself rather than for Sweden; rumour of a Saxon marriage for the young king; Auersperg flatters Sehested and has attached Windischgrätz to him to sound him out.

reading_review.by: project (the project's verification pass), after the contributor's own reader
reading_review.note: Read end to end as sentences: coherent chancery German (French in L27) that matches the contributor's summary. Grade B: no punctuation, period spelling, transcription by AI agents with no human check, and 20 of 314 tokens are holes by the strict count (probable or restored words, symbol values given by the sense, open symbols). The English text is a summary, not a translation.

texts.label: L02, to the king, Vienna 17/27 Jan. 1657
texts.summary: To the king: Sehested greeted Auersperg on the alliance and the 'secret'; Auersperg took it ad referendum, then reported that the Emperor is not averse to the defensive alliance proposed by the king but expects the draft and conditions from Denmark; the 'secret' once mentioned to Castel Rodrigo no longer matters. On 14/24 Jan Auersperg asked for haste and for the inclusion of the States General.

reading_review.by: Claude Opus 5.5 agent of Brice Dudout (one reader)
reading_review.note: Decoded text read letter by letter as German sentences; the words outside the period word list were checked one by one; five letters are confirmed by a second cipher copy and two by a clear of the time. Grade B: no human reader, transcription by AI agents only, and some 20 nomenclator symbols rest on the sense or are open. Integration note (12 Nov 2026): not re-read end to end by the project; the verification pass scored every letter as German with the key and re-decoded it. Strict count: 347 of 371 tokens read. The English text is a summary, not a translation.

texts.label: L03, to the king, Vienna 7/17 Feb. 1657 (date read 28/7; Gigas: 17 Feb.)
texts.summary: To the king: nothing new; spirits in Vienna raised by Rebolledo's favourable report on Danish armaments, passed to the Emperor by La Fuente on 2/12 Feb; passage through Friuli refused to the Turk; the Swiss rejected France's threefold proposal (Alsace); birth of an archduke on 1/11 Feb; Rákóczi advancing in Poland, Danzig seeking neutrality.

reading_review.by: project (the integration pass), after the contributor's own reader
reading_review.note: Read end to end as sentences: coherent chancery German (French in L27) that matches the contributor's summary. Grade B: no punctuation, period spelling, transcription by AI agents with no human check, and 11 of 255 tokens are holes by the strict count (probable or restored words, symbol values given by the sense, open symbols). The English text is a summary, not a translation (a full translation of this letter was added to translation.md at integration).

texts.label: L04, to the chancellor, Vienna 7/17 Feb. 1657 (with P.S.)
